title: Build a list of 30 African tech hubs and innovation centres that host cohorts by Fri Nov 27
description: Hubs such as co-working and innovation centres host bootcamps, fellowships and incubator cohorts and recommend tools to them. Different from the bootcamp, university and partnership lead lists: hubs are the venue, not the trainer. Done = 30 hubs across Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya with the programmes they host, the public contact for programmes or community, and a partnership offer draft (for example a hub workspace for resident cohorts) that the team approves before use.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Qualify 30 actual cohort-hosting hubs with dated programme and contact evidence
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build one deduplicated research list plus one unpublished partnership-offer draft, rather than another bootcamp list. First define eligibility: a physical innovation/coworking hub in Nigeria, Ghana or Kenya must have official evidence of hosting a named recurring or cohort programme; distinguish venue host, programme operator and training provider. Seed-source check on 22 October 2026: https://dev.ihub.co.ke/programs/ names programmes but includes 2023-2025 dates, so it is a lead to reverify, not proof of a current 2026 cohort. https://meltwater.org/mest-ai-startup-program/ documents residential training in Accra, which alone does not prove that it is a qualifying third-party host. This illustrates why directories and familiar brands cannot be accepted without role/date checks. For each accepted record provide hub name, city/country, official URL, named hosted programme and host relationship, programme/source date, public programmes/community enquiry route and source, fit reason, confidence and unresolved questions. Check existing bootcamp, institution and partnership lists for duplicates and tag shared organisations rather than invent new leads. Aim for balanced country coverage with 30 verified distinct records; report a shortfall and excluded candidates if evidence cannot support 30, rather than filling with trainers. Done: CSV plus source log, exclusions/dedup notes and a draft offer for the team to approve, with no workspace benefits, prices or discounts promised. Quality measure: each accepted row passes host/location/programme/contact evidence checks; every unknown is labelled and sources are re-opened before delivery. No outreach, personal-contact scraping or publication.

acceptedWorkstreams.description: Use a venue-and-programme evidence model: a hub qualifies only where its own public pages or the programme organiser identify a hosted cohort, fellowship or incubator programme; a trainer with no evidenced host role does not qualify. Cover Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya, deduplicate branches and parent organisations, and record host, hosted programme, date/status, public programme/community contact route, source URL and check date. Missing dates and sizes remain unknown. Rank by evidenced cohort activity and a practical buyer route, not invented reach. Deliver one coherent thirty-hub register plus a single proposed partner offer for a resident cohort and a short exclusions log, reusing existing bootcamp/university lists only for deduplication. Acceptance: thirty distinct qualifying hubs across the three countries; every hosted-programme assertion has direct evidence; each contact is publicly intended for business/programme enquiries; the offer makes no pricing, capacity or implementation promises without confirmation. If fewer than thirty qualify, report the exact shortfall instead of padding. Measure verified entries, evidence freshness, exclusions and pilot-readiness decisions. This supplies a specific qualification method absent from the current generic audit/execution proposal. No outreach, agreements, scraping of private contacts or invented partnerships.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Reachability register: give each qualified hub a public contact channel and a one-paragraph intro note, so the list becomes actionable
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted workstreams qualify which hubs actually host cohorts; this idea turns that list into something the team can act on next week. Approach: for each of the 30 qualified hubs, record the public contact channel (website contact form, public email, or LinkedIn page - never scraped personal data), the region, and a one-paragraph intro note that references the hub's own public cohort activity, so a first message never sounds like cold spam. Include one short forwarding email template the team can adapt, and mark any hub where no public contact exists. Done when: every hub row has a public contact channel or an explicit 'no public contact' flag, and the intro notes cite only what the hub itself publishes. Measured: 30 rows, each with contact channel and note; count of hubs with no public contact, as a follow-up target. Why this fits: the goal says hubs recommend tools to their cohorts, which only happens after someone reaches out; this adds the outreach-ready layer the qualification workstreams do not cover, without duplicating them.
